full_judgment: 8. Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of respondents made submissions in support of the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division. He also submitted that the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division considering the evidence and materials on record came to the decision that the judgment and decree passed by the lower appellate Court reversing the judgment and decree passed by the Trial Court is not a proper judgment of reversal inasmuch as the appellate Court has not adverted to all the findings arrived at by the trial Court as such the High Court Division rightly set aside the judgment and decree passed by the lower appellate Court and the judgment and decree dated 31-10-1992 passed by the Assistant Judge, Boalkhali, Chittagong in Other Class Suit No. 59 of 1990 have been restored rightly. He further submitted that the High Court Division after hearing the parties and considering the judgments and order of the courts below and also considering the evidence and materials on record came to the conclusion that the plaintiff did not claim any relief against the deed in question, she simply stated in her examination-in-chief that she has suffered loss by the deed in question. She did not adduce any evidence claiming the deed in question to be created by false personification and also held that the deed was executed and registered on commission and the deed having been executed and registered on commission there is no scope to say that the said deed was forged unless any positive evidence is adduced; that there was no evidence available on record to declare the deed to be a forged or void one, the learned Single Judge has held that the learned Sub-ordinate Judge now Joint District Judge being the last Court of fact committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in declaring the deed in question to be void as such the learned Single Judge rightly set aside the judgment and decree passed by the lower appellate Court which need not be interfered by this Court. He also submitted that the parties to the deed in question are the heirs and legal representatives of late Obaidur Rahman, so the deed has been in favour of the co-sharers of Obaidur Rahman by Obaidur Rahman himself, as such the High Court Division held that the plaintiffs may seek remedy in a properly instituted partition suit and made the Rule absolute in Civil Revision No. 2381 of 1996 which should not be interfered by this Division in this appeal. He lastly submitted that the High Court Division considering evidence of the plaintiffs witnesses and defendants witnesses and facts and circumstances of the case came to the finding that there is merit in the Rule, and accordingly made the Rule absolute, thus restoring the judgment and order of the trial Court dated 29th March, 2007, which should not be reversed in this appeal for ends of justice.
